decisions.reason: For B=k x k augmented by first projection and X=Spec k, adjoining a disjoint union of second-factor points of any cardinality gives flat locally finitely presented deformations with distinct isomorphism classes. Thus the unrestricted assertion of a set is false. The repair preserves arbitrary bases and qualifies smallness for nilpotent augmentation ideals.

F4 confuses the degree -1 free module F tensor_R B with the conormal module K/K^2, which is its quotient by the degree -2 differential. For instance a redundant two-generator presentation of K=(t) has F tensor_R k=k^2 but K/K^2=k. The main obstruction/torsor result follows independently from the exact source theorem F3, so this is nonfatal. F4 is corrected, and the flat specialization now exposes the arbitrary square-zero finiteness already proved in step 2.1.

On the rejected carrier, proof 1.1 and 2.1 use finite presentation of lifts over k[I] for arbitrary I, but the supplier Statement restricts this conclusion to small Artin extensions. Thus the correspondence between all ringed-space solutions and the stipulated locally finitely presented scheme deformations is unsupported by the cited interface. Repair is completed in the assigned supplier: its existing proof 2.1 establishes the needed arbitrary-square-zero result, now stated explicitly. The theorem F2 now records the precise arbitrary-square-zero finiteness application used by proof 1.1 and 2.1.

Dual numbers, arbitrary k[I], Artin bases, the trivial object and coefficient base change retain their interfaces. Stacks 29.22.2 (01TQ), full statement and proof consulted, verifies finite presentation on every affine chart.

Stacks 08SM supplies exactly the arbitrary N,c lifting problem and transitivity-boundary obstruction, plus the Ext1 torsor and Ext0 automorphisms. F4 now agrees with the complete 09AM construction and local supplier. For canonical N=B tensor_A I the conormal map is the identity, so 063Y gives flatness and exact base reduction for arbitrary square-zero I. Step 2.1 gives finite generators and J intersection IP prime=IJ by flatness; lifting reduced relations and I^2=0 yields finite presentation without any finiteness on I.

F2 now explicitly applies the corrected arbitrary-square-zero finite-presentation clause to k[I] for infinite-dimensional I, licensing proof 1.1 and 2.1. Stacks 08UX gives the global extension torsor without cover finiteness; 04EW turns extensions by quasi-coherent O_X tensor_k I into schemes, and 063Y gives precisely flat lifts. Corrected affine finiteness gives local finite presentation for arbitrary I. The trivial lift selects the origin, coefficient pushout agrees with base change, Ext0 gives identity-reducing derivations, and finite locally free Ext gives H1(T) for smooth X. The assigned manifest strategy is corrected from N=I to N=B tensor_k I and synchronized with the actual global proof; the public Statement and numbered proof steps are unchanged.
